checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.54pp larger on average (188 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: STATISTICAL REALITY: 'measured ghost arrival = 25.6 control trades/day', used together with 'confirm planned n = 600' to imply the confirm samples are reachable.
findings.problem: The live tier in DATA contains 25 events in total over a 61.0-day span, and control's live_n is 4 (with 4 of the 26 open trades attributed to it). A 25.6-trades-per-day arrival rate cannot be reconciled with 25 live events ever recorded; the figure must be a backfill-derived rate being presented as 'measured'. Every timeline claim about reaching n=600 on live tape rests on it.

findings.claim: Checklist 'bonferroni_monotonic' is green: 'lifetime tests=6, pre-registered hypotheses=6; alpha=0.00833 — Corrected bar counts every question asked'.
findings.problem: The graveyard_enforced check reports 46 refutations loaded, i.e. 46 questions this project has already asked and answered, and the retired arms (dedup-0h/2h/24h/48h, sl-entry-anchor) were each tested and killed. Counting only 6 lifetime tests does not count every question asked. It is also internally inconsistent: the L-sl-entry-anchor kill record states its paired p was judged against alpha=0.01250, not the 0.00833 quoted here, so two different divisors are in use and the check verifies neither.

findings.claim: Checklist 'entry_granularity_declared': 'Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel.'
findings.problem: Sharing the kernel only neutralises the +0.54pp pump overstatement for arms that do not move a detection threshold. entry-8pct changes pump_pct to 8.0 and vol-4x changes vol_threshold to 4.0, and their scored samples (screen_n=494 and 861) differ from control's 1541 precisely because the threshold selects events. A systematic +0.54pp bias in the measured pump lands differentially on a threshold-moving arm, so the bias does not cancel in exactly the two comparisons that need it most.

findings.claim: Checklist 'arms_running' is green with detail '5 running: tp-7pct, hold-12h, entry-8pct, sl-5pct, vol-4x'.
findings.problem: The arena listing marks control and placebo as [running/confirm] as well, so the running count in the checkbox does not match the arena state it is meant to verify. Separately, entry-8pct is counted as a running confirm arm on live_n=1 — one resolved live trade — which is a running label backed by essentially no live tape.

findings.claim: Checklist 'paired_population' is green: '4789 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them.'
findings.problem: sl-5pct (screen_n=1540) and tp-7pct (screen_n=1540) are scored on fewer events than control and placebo (screen_n=1541), yet sl_pct and tp_pct are exit parameters that cannot remove a detection from the population. The one-event asymmetry is unexplained by the changed= dict, and the open-trade dict (sl-5pct 5, tp-7pct 5 vs control 4) shows the divergence is in resolution, not detection. 'Every arm has seen all of them' is asserted at the event level while the scored n's differ.

findings.claim: Arm headlines quote screen_dWR as the achievement: sl-5pct screen_dWR=5.26pp, hold-12h screen_dWR=3.18pp.
findings.problem: These deltas come from the screen/backfill tier (4764 backfill events vs 25 live), while the arms are labelled confirm with live_n=3 and live_n=4 — no live counterpart exists to support them. Worse for the fixed objective, which is win rate AND EV per trade: sl-5pct's screen_ev is 0.022 against control's 0.029, so the arm with the largest advertised win-rate gain is simultaneously below control on EV, and the dWR headline does not carry that.
